positions.text: Ouyang and coauthors operationalize RLHF as three linked stages: supervised fine-tuning, reward-model training from labeler-ranked outputs, and PPO optimization against that reward model. This directly supports the protected pipeline description within the InstructGPT design. The correspondence should remain bounded. It does not establish that every later preference-optimization method uses an explicit reward model or PPO, and it does not by itself validate the broader RLRF proposal.
scope_conditions: the canonical RLHF pipeline described by the cited literature

positions.text: Gao, Schulman, and Hilton show the central Goodhart problem in reward-model optimization: an imperfect proxy can improve under optimization while ground-truth performance worsens. This supports the protected overoptimization claim in their controlled synthetic setup. The result should not be overstated. Their gold-standard reward model stands in for humans, and the abstract does not establish that degradation is monotonic in realized KL distance from the reference policy.
scope_conditions: the scaling-law setting documented by Gao, Schulman, and Hilton

current_debate.name: In Gao, Schulman, and Hilton's synthetic proxy-versus-gold reward-model setup, optimizing an imperfect proxy too much can hinder ground-truth performance.

source_provenance.exactEvidenceQuote: In reinforcement learning from human feedback, it is common to optimize against a reward model trained to predict human preferences. Because the reward model is an imperfect proxy, optimizing its value too much can hinder ground truth performance, in accordance with Goodhart's law.
